principle: Coverage truth: only scenarios with a runner that passes in the unit suite count as executable.

status_definitions.executable_now: A deterministic, offline runner drives the scenario against Hawk AI's own control and the unit suite asserts the expected outcome and its evidence.
status_definitions.expected_gap: The runner executes, but Hawk AI does not produce the outcome the catalogue expects; the observed outcome is asserted so the gap stays visible. Not counted as executable.
status_definitions.requires_environment: Needs a system outside Hawk AI (see environment_requirements). Not counted as executable.

expected_gaps.reason: The catalogue expects the instruction attack to be sanitised and passed on (modify/redact). Hawk AI has no in-line prompt-sanitisation response for instruction attacks: the gateway and the browser control block them outright (stricter than expected).

The catalogue expects a sensitive upload summary to be allowed with a warning. Hawk AI holds personal data sent to an internal assistant for approval and blocks it towards an external one; there is no allow-with-warning path for sensitive uploads (stricter than expected).

The catalogue expects the runtime agent-action control to hold this attack for approval. Hawk AI blocks it outright (token, scope, chain-depth or target checks deny it), and even a valid identity acting on personal data is escalated to block by the central control engine; the only agent step-up path is an AI system still awaiting governance approval (stricter than expected).

The catalogue expects the MCP gateway to hold this agent request for approval. MCP authorisation fails closed: without a persisted purpose session that requires human confirmation the request is denied, so there is no step-up path for this attack at the MCP gateway (stricter than expected).

The catalogue expects the downgraded / tampered model to be denied. The gateway holds open-weight and self-hosted models for approval instead of denying them, and it cannot see the model's safety profile or artifact digest (no model-registry integration).

The gateway has no approved-model or provider allow-list: an unknown provider name, an endpoint impersonating a managed provider, or a silently changed model version is classified as a managed provider and allowed. Only open-weight / self-hosted models are held for approval.

No cost or usage guardrail exists on the monitoring surface: a usage-spike signal is ingested and stored, but no threshold turns it into a warning or a block (COST_GUARDRAIL / RESOURCE_THROTTLING are not implemented for telemetry). The runner records that no enforcement decision is produced.

No output-grounding or uncertainty control: the gateway does not check that a model's justification is backed by evidence or that an uncertain answer is flagged, so a fabricated justification or an overconfident answer is allowed. (Decisions that involve personal data are held for human approval, which the step-up variants test.)

environment_requirements.requirement: An OCR engine on the API host (the tesseract binary used through pytesseract) to read text out of the uploaded image; it is not part of the API image or the unit-test environment.

A connected model registry (for example MLflow, SageMaker Model Registry, Azure ML or Hugging Face Hub) exposing model artifact digests, versions, providers and safety profiles to Hawk AI through a connector; Hawk AI has no model-registry connector, so the connector surface cannot be exercised offline.
